## ACF

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/acf>

Integrate ACF with Registration Forms | URM Docs

# ACF
Pro Learn how to integrate Advanced Custom Fields (ACF) with User Registration Pro to seamlessly map and display custom user data in registration forms.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

# Integrating Advanced Custom Fields (ACF) with User Registration

Would you like to display custom user data from ACF fields in your User Registration forms? User Registration & Membership allows you to map registration form fields to ACF custom fields, so user data flows seamlessly between both plugins.

This tutorial will show you how to connect User Registration Pro forms with ACF custom fields by creating ACF field groups and mapping them through the usermeta table.

**Requirements:** This feature requires the User Registration Pro plugin .

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated both the User Registration Pro plugin and the Advanced Custom Fields plugin on your WordPress site.

## Installing Advanced Custom Fields

To begin, you'll need the ACF plugin installed on your site.

Go to **Plugins → Add New** in your WordPress dashboard. Search for "Advanced Custom Fields" and click **Install Now**, then **Activate**.

Once activated, you'll see a new **ACF** menu item in your WordPress admin sidebar.

## Creating ACF Field Groups

Next, you'll create custom fields in ACF that will store your user data.

Navigate to **ACF → Field Groups** and click **Add New**. Enter a name for your field group — this helps you organize related fields together.

Click **Add Field** to create your first custom field.

You'll need to configure two key settings:

**Field Label**: The display name for your field (e.g., "Phone Number")

**Field Type**: The type of data this field will store (e.g., Text, Number, Email)

ACF automatically generates a **Field Name** when you create a field. You'll need this exact field name later when mapping to User Registration fields.

Scroll down to the **Settings** section. Under **Location Rules**, set where this field should appear. For user data, select **User Form** and choose the appropriate user context (e.g., Add / Edit).

Click **Save Changes** to save your field group.

## Mapping User Registration Fields to ACF

Now you'll connect your User Registration form fields to the ACF fields you just created.

Go to **User Registration → All Forms** and select the form you want to map. Click **Edit** to open the form builder.

Navigate to **Form Editor → Form Settings → Advanced **in the form settings.

Enable the option to **map form fields with external fields**. This unlocks the field mapping interface.

Select **Usermeta Table** as the mapping destination. This is where both User Registration and ACF store custom user data.

In the **Form Fields** section, select the User Registration fields you want to map. Click the **+** button to add multiple field mappings.

In the **External Field keys** section, enter the ACF **Field Name** for each corresponding field. These must match exactly — copy them directly from your ACF field settings.

**Tip:** To find the exact ACF Field Name, go back to **ACF → Field Groups**, edit your field group, and look at the Field Name value for each field.

Click **Update** to save your form mapping.

## Testing the Integration

Once mapped, data flows automatically between User Registration and ACF.

When a user registers through your User Registration form, the data they enter will be stored in the usermeta table and automatically synced to your ACF fields.

You can verify this by:

Submitting a test registration through your form

Going to **Users → All Users** in WordPress

Editing the test user

Scrolling down to see your ACF fields populated with the registration data

## ActiveCampaign

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/activecampaign>

ActiveCampaign Integration in User Registration & Membership

# ActiveCampaign
Pro Automatically sync WordPress user registrations with ActiveCampaign email lists using API integration to add subscribers without manual imports.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to automatically add new users to your ActiveCampaign email lists when they register on your site? User Registration & Membership allows you to sync registration data directly with ActiveCampaign, so every new signup becomes a subscriber without manual imports. This tutorial will show you how to connect ActiveCampaign to your registration forms and map form fields to your ActiveCampaign lists.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin. Then, make sure you've installed and activated the ActiveCampaign addon from User Registration & Membership → Addons.

## Getting Your ActiveCampaign API Credentials

To connect User Registration & Membership with ActiveCampaign, you'll need your API Key and API URL from your ActiveCampaign account. From your ActiveCampaign dashboard, go to Settings → Developer to access your API credentials. Here, you'll see your API URL and API Key. Copy both of these - you'll need them in the next step.

How to get the ActiveCampaign API Key and URL? - Official Documentation

## Connecting Your ActiveCampaign Account

Once you have your API credentials, go to User Registration & Membership → Settings → Integration → ActiveCampaign.

Enter your ActiveCampaign URL in the first field, then paste your API Key in the second field. Give your connection a name — this is just for your reference if you connect multiple ActiveCampaign accounts. Then, click the **Connect** button to link your account.

Once connected, you'll see a confirmation message. You can add multiple ActiveCampaign accounts by repeating this process. If you need to disconnect an account later, click the **Disconnect** button next to the account name.

## Linking ActiveCampaign to a Registration Form

Now that your ActiveCampaign account is connected, you can link it to any registration form. Go to User Registration & Membership → All Forms and click **Edit** on the form you want to connect. Navigate to **Form Settings → Integration → ActiveCampaign**, then click **Add Connection**.

Give this connection a nickname — this is just for your reference and won't be visible to users. Then, click **Add Connection** to continue.

## Mapping Form Fields to ActiveCampaign

After creating the connection, you'll see options to map your registration form fields to ActiveCampaign list fields. From the **Select Account** dropdown, choose which connected ActiveCampaign account to use if you have multiple accounts configured. Then, select the ActiveCampaign list where you want to send registration data from the **Select List** dropdown.

Next, map your form fields to the corresponding ActiveCampaign fields. The email field mapping is required — select which form field contains the user's email address. You can also map additional fields like first name, last name, and any custom fields you've created in ActiveCampaign. User Registration & Membership supports up to 100 field mappings per connection.

Once you've mapped all the fields you need, click **Save Changes** to activate the integration.

## Using Conditional Logic (Optional)

If you'd like to control when users are added to ActiveCampaign based on their form responses, enable **Use Conditional Logic**. This allows you to create rules that only send data to ActiveCampaign when specific conditions are met — for example, only adding users who select a particular checkbox or choose a specific option from a dropdown.

To set up conditional logic, toggle on **Use Conditional Logic** and configure your rules based on form field values. Be sure to check out our guide on using conditional logic with integrations for complete details.

## How the Integration Works

Once the integration is active, new users who register through your form will automatically be added to your selected ActiveCampaign list. The integration works with standard registration forms, WooCommerce checkout forms, and the user Account Page. Contact details sync for both new and existing users whenever they register or update their information.

If you're using membership plans, you can sync membership data alongside contact information. ActiveCampaign's site tracking capabilities also work with registered users, allowing you to monitor how they interact with your site and campaigns.

That's it! Now you know how to connect ActiveCampaign to your registration forms and automatically build your email lists. Next, would you like to learn about other email marketing integrations? Be sure to check out our guides on MailChimp, MailerLite, and Kit integrations for more options.

## Brevo

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/brevo>

Connect Brevo to User Registration & Membership | URM Docs

# Brevo
Pro Learn how to automatically sync new member registrations with your Brevo email lists using the User Registration & Membership plugin's Brevo addon integration.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to automatically add new members to your Brevo email lists when they register on your site? User Registration & Membership allows you to sync registration data directly with Brevo (formerly Sendinblue), so you can build your email marketing lists and send targeted campaigns without manual data entry. This tutorial will show you how to connect your Brevo account and map form fields to your email lists.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you've installed and activated the Brevo addon.

## Activating the Brevo Addon

To connect with Brevo, you'll first need to activate the Brevo addon. From your WordPress dashboard, go to **User Registration & Membership → Addons**. Here, you'll see a list of all available addons for your plan.

Locate the Brevo addon in the list and toggle the switch to **Activate**. Once activated, the Brevo integration settings will become available in your plugin settings.

To set up the User Registration Brevo integration on your site, you will have to go to the following location.

User Registration & Membership > Settings > Integrations > Brevo.

As you can see, you will need the Brevo API key to complete this integration. Let us look at how to generate the API key.

## Generating a Brevo API key

Log in or Sign Up to your Brevo account.

Click on your name at the top-right side of the screen.

Click **SMTP & API**

Under the **API keys** tab, click **Generate a new API key**.

Name your API key.

Click **Generate**.

Copy your API key and **save it** somewhere safe.

Your API v3 key is only visible during this time.

## Integrating Brevo with User Registration & Membership

Once you have generated and copied the API key, go to

User Registration > Settings > Integration > Brevo(ex Sendinblue)

Now, enter the API key and give a name to the connection and hit **Connect.**

Once the connection is successful, you will see the above set up. You can click on the **Disconnect **button to remove the connection.

You can add multiple Brevo connections.

### Connecting Registration Forms to Brevo

After successfully setting up the Brevo API connection, now you can send user data to your Brevo list via the User Registration registration forms.

Go to **User Registration > All Forms**.

Choose to edit the desired form.

Go to **Form Settings > Integrations > Brevo**.

Now, choose the Brevo account(if multiple accounts are connected), select the desired list and then map the form fields to their respective fields to send the user data.

Click on **Update Form** and you are good to go.

Now, whenever a user registers via this form, their data are sent to the selected Brevo list.

To create a Bevo list, log in to your Brevo account, go to Contacts > Lists and click on Create a List.

#### Using Double Opt-in

You can use the Double Opt-in option to send the data by enabling it from the connection settings in each individual form's connection. You will need to set up the following attributes for this.

**Double Optin Template:** Select the desired template created at your Brevo account for the Double Optin.

**Redirection URL:** Set a redirection URL for the users to be redirected if chosen the Double Optin method.

#### Using Conditional Logic

You can use conditional logic while sending the data to the Brevo list. For this, enable the 'Use Conditional Logic' option on the 'Connection' settings for each individual form

## BuddyPress

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/buddypress>

BuddyPress Integration for User Registration & Membership

# BuddyPress
Pro Automatically sync user registration form data with BuddyPress profile fields to eliminate duplicate data entry and streamline member onboarding.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to connect your User Registration & Membership forms with BuddyPress to sync user profile data automatically?

User Registration & Membership allows you to map registration form fields to BuddyPress profile fields, so member information flows seamlessly between the two plugins. This guide will show you how to set up and configure the BuddyPress integration.

## Prerequisites

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership plugin on your WordPress site. You'll also need to have the BuddyPress plugin installed and activated, with at least one BuddyPress profile field group created.

## Understanding BuddyPress Field Mapping

User Registration & Membership includes a field mapping feature that synchronizes form data with external plugins like BuddyPress. When enabled, data entered into your registration forms automatically populates the corresponding BuddyPress profile fields, eliminating the need for users to enter the same information twice.

The mapping works by connecting User Registration form fields to BuddyPress profile field meta keys. Once configured, every new registration or profile update syncs the data to BuddyPress automatically.

### **Create a custom profile field**

The Profile Details section of BuddyPress can be customized using a tool. You may get to it by heading to **Users > Profile Fields** in the WordPress administration section. Name (Primary), the sole field that is displayed by default, is a field that must be filled up. This information is used to identify a person on the website; it appears at the top of their profile and in activity items.

Profile fields can collect a variety of information from your users. BuddyPress offers the following field types: text box, multi-line text box, date selector, radio buttons, drop-down select box, multi-select box, and checkboxes. Let’s add a checkbox field to collect your users’ favorite musicians upon signup. First, click on the “**Add New Field**” button.

Add the “**field title**” (which serves as the registration form’s label) and the “**field description**” (which, if not empty, serves as explanatory text), determined that this field is not required, and entered your first musician choice.

You might need more options, so you can click the link “**Add another option**” to add more options until you’re satisfied.

You can also select a few other options for the profile field like visibility, required or not, and an option to enable the use of this field in the BuddyPress registration form.

## Enabling Field Mapping for BuddyPress

To set up BuddyPress integration, you'll need to enable the field mapping feature on your registration form.

Go to **User Registration & Membership → All Forms → Registration Forms** and select the form you want to configure. Then, navigate to **Form Settings → Advanced**.

Toggle on **Enable Form Field Mapping With External Fields**. This activates the mapping functionality for the form.

**Here, you can select two types of tables:Usermeta Table:** This is the default WordPress wp_usermenta table. Select the form fields and write the field keys(from the external plugin) on the available fields respectively.

**External Table**: If any of the external plugins create their own table, you will have to use this option. For example, in the case of BuddyPress, it creates its own table on the database.

Table Name: Select the required table name for the external plugin. In the case of BuddyPress, select wp_bp_xprofile_data

Column for User ID: Select ‘user_id’.

Column for Field Key: Select ‘field_id’.

Column for Field Value: Select ‘value’

Now, choose the User Registration ‘checkbox’ field on the left and write the field key for the checkbox field on the BuddyPress registration form. Hit ‘**Update Form**.

You can now register a user via the User Registration form and that user will have the checkbox field mapped in his/her BuddyPress Member account page.

## Important Notes About BuddyPress Mapping

Field mapping is configured per individual form, not globally. If you have multiple registration forms, you'll need to set up mapping for each one separately.

You must know the exact meta keys used by BuddyPress for each profile field. Incorrect meta keys will prevent data from syncing properly.

The mapping works with the default WordPress **usermeta** table, which is where BuddyPress stores profile data by default.

Field types should be compatible between User Registration and BuddyPress for proper syncing. For example, text fields should map to text fields, and date fields should map to date fields.

## Cloud Storage

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/cloud-storage>

Cloud Storage

# Cloud Storage
Pro Integrate Dropbox or Google Drive to automatically backup files uploaded through registration forms to your cloud storage account.
Last updated on Aug 13, 2026

Would you like to automatically send user-uploaded files from registration forms directly to Dropbox or Google Drive? User Registration & Membership allows you to integrate cloud storage services, so every file uploaded through your forms is automatically backed up to your cloud account. This tutorial will show you how to set up cloud storage integration step by step.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you've installed and activated the Cloud Storage add-on.

## Installing the Cloud Storage Add-on

To install the Cloud Storage add-on, go to **User Registration & Membership > Addons**. Locate the **Cloud Storage add-on** and toggle the switch to Activate.

## Setting Up Dropbox Integration

The Dropbox integration allows you to connect User Registration & Membership with your Dropbox account and store uploaded files in Dropbox.

Follow the steps below to create a Dropbox app, configure OAuth 2.0, connect your Dropbox account, and configure the upload folder.

### 1. Create a Dropbox App

First, log in to your Dropbox account and open the Dropbox Developer Platform .

Click **App Console**.

Click **Create app**.

Select **Scoped App**.

Select the appropriate access type for your integration.

Enter a name for your app.

Click **Create app**.

Dropbox uses scopes to control what your application can access. Select only the permissions required by the integration.

### 2. Configure OAuth 2.0

After creating the app, open the **Settings** tab and locate the **OAuth 2** section.

Under **Redirect URIs**, enter your website URL.

For example:

`https://example.com/`

Click **Add** to save the redirect URI.

The redirect URI configured in Dropbox must exactly match the URI used by the integration. Dropbox verifies the redirect URI during the OAuth authorization process.

For more information, see the Dropbox OAuth 2 Guide .

### 3. Get the App Key and App Secret

In the **Settings** tab, locate the **App key** and **App secret**.

Copy both values. You will need them when connecting Dropbox to User Registration & Membership.

### 4. Connect Dropbox to User Registration & Membership

In your WordPress dashboard, go to:

**User Registration & Membership → Settings → Integration → Cloud Storage**

Then:

Open the **Dropbox** tab.

Enter your **App Key**.

Enter your **App Secret**.

Click **Save Changes**.

Click **Connect with Dropbox**.

Sign in to Dropbox if prompted.

Review and authorize the requested permissions.

After authorization is completed, you will be redirected back to your website and the Dropbox connection will be established.

### 5. Configure the Dropbox Upload Folder

Once Dropbox is connected, configure the folder where uploaded files should be stored.

Enter the desired folder path in the **Folder Path** field.

For example:

`/UserRegistrationFiles`

The folder path should start with a forward slash (`/`).

If the specified folder does not exist, Dropbox will create it automatically.

### 6. Verify the Connection

After completing the configuration, upload a file through a User Registration & Membership form that uses file upload functionality.

Check your Dropbox account and verify that the uploaded file appears in the configured folder.

For additional information about Dropbox app configuration, see the Dropbox Getting Started Guide .

## Setting Up Google Drive Integration

Follow the steps below to connect Google Drive with User Registration & Membership and configure it as your cloud storage provider.

### 1. Create a Google Cloud Project

Log in to the Google Cloud Console and create a new project.

Click **Create Project**.

Enter a name for your project.

Click **Create**.

Once the project is created, select it from the project dropdown at the top of the page.

### 2. Enable the Google Drive API

After creating your project, enable the Google Drive API.

In the Google Cloud Console, go to **APIs & Services → Library**.

Search for **Google Drive API**.

Select **Google Drive API** from the search results.

Click **Enable**.

### 3. Configure the OAuth Consent Screen

Before creating OAuth credentials, configure the OAuth consent screen for your application.

Go to **Google Auth Platform** or **APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen**, depending on the Google Cloud Console interface.

Select the appropriate user type.

Enter your application name and required application information.

Configure the required scopes and test users if prompted.

Save the configuration.

**Note:** Google may require additional verification or test-user configuration depending on the type of Google account and scopes used by your application.

### 4. Create OAuth Credentials

After configuring the consent screen, create OAuth credentials.

Go to **APIs & Services → Credentials**.

Click **Create Credentials**.

Select **OAuth client ID**.

Choose **Web application** as the application type.

Add your site URL to the **Authorized JavaScript origins** field.

Add your redirect URL to the **Authorized redirect URIs** field.

The redirect URL should be your site URL followed by:

`/wp-admin/admin.php`

For example:

`https://example.com/wp-admin/admin.php`

Click **Create**.

Google will generate your OAuth credentials. Copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret**.

### 5. Connect Google Drive to User Registration & Membership

In your WordPress dashboard, go to:

**User Registration & Membership → Settings → Integration → Cloud Storage**

Then:

Select the **Google Drive** tab.

Enter your **Client ID**.

Enter your **Client Secret**.

Click **Save Changes**.

Click **Connect with Google Drive**.

Select your Google account when prompted.

Review and grant the requested permissions.

After authorization is complete, you will be redirected back to your website and a success message will be displayed.

### 6. Configure Google Drive Upload Settings

After connecting Google Drive, configure the folder where uploaded files should be stored.

Enter the desired **Folder Name** in the Google Drive upload settings.

For example:

`UserRegistrationFiles`

This will create or use a folder named **UserRegistrationFiles** in the root directory of your Google Drive.

If the specified folder does not exist, Google Drive will create it automatically.

## Testing Your Cloud Storage Integration

To verify that your Google Drive integration is working correctly:

Create a test registration form.

Add a **File Upload** field to the form.

Configure the form and publish it.

Submit the form with a test file.

Open your connected Google Drive account.

Navigate to the configured folder.

Verify that the uploaded file appears in the folder.

You can follow the same process to test your Dropbox integration.

That's it! Your Google Drive cloud storage integration is now configured and ready to store files uploaded through your registration forms.

For more information, see the and .

## Divi Builder Integration

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/divi-builder-integration>

Divi Builder Integration for Registration Forms | URM Docs

# Divi Builder Integration
Create visually stunning registration and membership pages using Divi Builder's drag-and-drop interface without writing any code.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to design beautiful registration and membership pages without touching code? User Registration & Membership integrates directly with Divi Builder, allowing you to drag and drop registration forms, login forms, and membership features into your Divi-powered pages.

This guide will show you how to use Divi's visual editor to customize your user registration, login, profile, and membership pages.

## Prerequisites

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the following:

**User Registration & Membership plugin** (v4.1.4 or higher)

**Divi Theme** or **Divi Builder plugin**

WordPress admin access

If you're using the Divi Theme, the Divi Builder is already included—you don't need to install the plugin separately.

## Installing the Required Plugins

### Installing User Registration & Membership

From your WordPress dashboard, go to **Plugins → Add New Plugin**

Search for "User Registration & Membership"

Click **Install Now**, then **Activate**

Alternatively, if you have the Pro version:

Go to **Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin**

Upload the User Registration & Membership Pro zip file

Click **Install Now**, then **Activate**

### Installing Divi Builder

If you don't already have Divi installed:

**For Divi Theme:**

Go to **Appearance → Themes → Add New Theme**

Click **Upload Theme**

Upload the Divi theme zip file

Click **Install**, then **ActivateFor Divi Builder Plugin:**

Go to **Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin**

Upload the Divi Builder plugin zip file

Click **Install Now**, then **Activate**

You can purchase Divi Builder from the official Divi website.

## Adding User Registration Modules to Divi Pages

User Registration & Membership provides several Divi modules that you can add to any page. All modules are prefixed with "URM" for easy identification.

### Step 1: Open the Divi Builder

Navigate to **Pages** in your WordPress dashboard

Find the page you want to edit

Hover below the page name and click **Edit with Divi**

The Divi Builder visual editor will open.

### Step 2: Add a New Section

Click the blue **+** sign to add a new section to your page

Click the green **+** sign to insert a row layout

Choose your preferred column structure

### Step 3: Insert a User Registration Module

Click the black **+** sign under the row to insert a module

Scroll down to find User Registration & Membership modules

All URM modules start with the "URM" prefix

**Available URM Modules:URM Registration Form** — Display registration forms

**URM Login Form** — Display login forms

**URM Frontend Listing** — Display member directories

**URM Popup** — Display popup forms

**URM Download PDF Button** — Add PDF download functionality (requires PDF Submission addon)

### Step 4: Configure the Module

When you select a module, a settings pop-up will appear with three tabs:

#### Content Tab

**Form/Component Selection:** Choose which registration form, login form, or component to display

**User State:** Configure user state settings (options vary by module)

Module-specific options depending on which URM module you selected

#### Design Tab

Modify visual appearance including colors, fonts, spacing, and borders

Customize the module's design to match your site branding

#### Advanced Tab

Add CSS ID & Classes for custom styling

Add Custom CSS for advanced customization

Configure Transitions and animations

Set Visibility conditions

### Step 5: Save Your Changes

Click the green checkmark to save the module settings

Optionally, you can:

Duplicate the module

Add the module to your Divi Library for reuse

Lock the module to prevent accidental changes

### Step 6: Publish the Page

Once you've finished setting up all modules, click **Save** and exit the Divi Builder. Your registration or membership page is now live.

## Example: Creating a Registration Page with Divi

Here's a complete example of building a registration page:

Create a new page or edit an existing one

Click **Edit with Divi**

Add a new section with a single-column row

Insert the **URM Registration Form** module

In the Content tab, select your registration form from the dropdown

In the Design tab, customize colors and spacing to match your site

Add a heading module above the form with a welcome message

Save and publish the page

## Example: Adding a Login Popup with Divi

If you have the URM Pro plugin with popups created:

Edit your page with Divi Builder

Add the **URM Popup** module where you want the trigger button

In the Content tab:

Select which popup to display from the **Popup** dropdown

Toggle **Use as Button** to "On"

Enter your **Button Text** (e.g., "Sign In")

In the Design tab, style the button to match your site

Save the module

When visitors click the button, your login popup will appear.

## Example: Adding a Member Directory with Divi

If you have the Frontend Listing addon active:

Edit your page with Divi Builder

Add the **URM Frontend Listing** module

In the Content tab, select your frontend listing from the **Frontend Listing** dropdown

Customize the design in the Design tab

Save and publish

You must create frontend listings first before they appear in the dropdown. If the Frontend Listing addon is not active, you'll see an error message.

## Example: Adding a PDF Download Button with Divi

If you have the PDF Submission addon active:

Edit your page with Divi Builder

Add the **URM Download PDF Button** module

In the Content tab, toggle **Preview** to "On" to see how the button looks while editing

Customize the button design in the Design tab

Save the module

Visitors can click the button to download PDF versions of their registration submissions.

This module requires the PDF Submission addon to be active. If it's not installed, you'll see an error message.

## Important Notes

**Module Options Vary:** The available settings in each URM module depend on which module you select. Registration forms have different options than login forms or member directories.

**Pro Features:** Some URM modules and features require User Registration & Membership Pro. Check your plan to see which integrations are available.

**Additional Integrations:** User Registration & Membership Pro also integrates with WooCommerce, Zapier, and other third-party services for extended functionality.

## Google Sheets

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/google-sheets>

Google Sheets Integration for User Registration & Membership

# Google Sheets
Pro Automatically sync WordPress user registration data to Google Sheets in real-time with secure OAuth authentication and custom field mapping.
Last updated on Jul 21, 2026

Would you like to automatically send user registration data from your WordPress forms to Google Spreadsheets? User Registration & Membership allows you to connect your registration forms to Google Sheets, so every new signup is instantly logged in a spreadsheet you can access, analyze, and share.

This tutorial will show you how to set up the Google Sheets integration, authenticate your Google account, and map your form fields to spreadsheet columns.

## Prerequisites

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you've installed and activated the Google Sheets addon from **User Registration & Membership → Addons**.

**Requirements:** The Google Sheets addon requires the Plus or Professional plan.

## Setting Up Google Cloud Console

To connect User Registration & Membership with Google Sheets, you'll need to create OAuth credentials in the Google Cloud Console. This allows the plugin to securely access your Google Sheets on your behalf.

### Creating a Google Cloud Project

Go to https://console.cloud.google.com/ and sign in with your Google account.

If you don't have an existing project, click **Select a project** at the top of the page, then click **New Project**.

Enter a project name and organization (if applicable), then click **Create**.

Once your project is created, make sure it's selected in the project dropdown at the top of the page.

### Enabling the Google Sheets API

From the Google Cloud Console dashboard, navigate to **API & Services → Library**.

In the API Library, search for **Google Sheets API** and click on it. Then, click the **Enable** button to activate the API for your project.

### Configuring the OAuth Consent Screen

Before you can create credentials, you need to configure the OAuth consent screen. This is the screen users see when they authorize the plugin to access their Google Sheets.

Navigate to **API & Services → OAuth consent screen**.

Select **External** as the user type, then click **Create**.

On the next screen, enter the following information:

**Application Name:** Enter a name for your application (e.g., "User Registration Integration")

**User Support Email:** Enter your email address

**Developer contact information:** Enter your email address (this can be the same as the User Support Email)

Click **Save and Continue** to proceed through the remaining steps. You can leave the optional fields blank.

Once you've completed the setup, click **Publish App** from the OAuth Consent Screen page to make your app functional.

You must publish the OAuth app for the integration to work. Unpublished apps will not authenticate properly.

### Creating OAuth Credentials

Navigate to **API & Services → Credentials** and click **Create Credentials** at the top of the page.

Select **OAuth Client ID** from the dropdown menu.

On the next screen, select **Web Application** as the application type.

Enter a name for your OAuth client (e.g., "User Registration Google Sheets").

Under **Authorized redirect URIs**, click **Add URI** and enter the following URL, replacing `yoursite.com` with your actual domain:

Text JavaScript TypeScript JSX TSX JSON PHP Python Bash HTML CSS SCSS SQL YAML Markdown Go Java Ruby Rust
`https://yoursite.com/wp-admin/admin.php?page=user-registration-settings&tab=integration&section=google-sheets`

**Important:** The redirect URI must exactly match this pattern for your domain. Make sure to include `https://` and the full path.

Click **Create** to generate your credentials.

A popup will appear with your **Client ID** and **Client Secret**. Copy both of these values — you'll need them in the next step.

## Connecting Google Sheets to User Registration

Now that you have your OAuth credentials, you can connect Google Sheets to the User Registration & Membership plugin.

In your WordPress dashboard, go to **User Registration & Membership → Settings → Integration → Google Sheets**.

Paste your **Client ID** and **Client Secret** into the corresponding fields.

Click **Connect** to authenticate with Google. You'll be redirected to Google's authorization page.

Sign in with your Google account and grant the requested permissions. Once authorized, you'll be redirected back to your WordPress site.

Click **Verify Access Code** to complete the connection.

## Mapping Form Fields to Google Sheets

With the integration connected, you can now configure which registration forms send data to Google Sheets and how that data is organized.

### Creating a Google Sheets Connection

Go to **User Registration & Membership → All Forms** and select the form you want to connect to Google Sheets.

Navigate to **Form Settings → Google Sheets** and click the **Add New Sheet** button.

You'll need the **Sheet ID** from your Google Sheets URL. Open the Google Sheets spreadsheet you want to use and copy the ID from the URL. The Sheet ID is the long string of characters between `/d/` and `/edit` in the URL.

For example, in this URL:

Text JavaScript TypeScript JSX TSX JSON PHP Python Bash HTML CSS SCSS SQL YAML Markdown Go Java Ruby Rust
`https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ABC123xyz456/edit`

The Sheet ID is `1ABC123xyz456`.

Paste the Sheet ID into the field and click **Add Sheet**.

### Mapping Fields to Columns

Once you've added the sheet, you'll see a field mapping interface. This is where you match your User Registration form fields to the columns in your Google Sheets spreadsheet.

For each form field you want to send to Google Sheets, select the corresponding column from the dropdown menu. The column names come from the first row of your spreadsheet.

The Sheet Name in Google Sheets doesn't need to match your form name — the integration uses the Sheet ID to identify the correct spreadsheet.

Click **Update Form** to save your field mapping.

## Testing the Integration

To verify the integration is working correctly, submit a test registration through your form.

After submission, open your Google Sheets spreadsheet and check that the new row contains the data from your test registration.

If the data doesn't appear, check the following:

Verify your OAuth credentials are correct in **User Registration & Membership → Settings → Integration → Google Sheets**

Confirm the Sheet ID is correct in your form settings

Make sure the column names in your spreadsheet match the field mappings

Check that your Google Sheets API is enabled in the Google Cloud Console

## Kit

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/kit>

Connect Kit to User Registration & Membership

# Kit
Pro Automatically sync new member registrations with Kit (ConvertKit) email lists to build your audience and run targeted campaigns without manual data entry.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to automatically add new members to your Kit email lists when they register on your site? User Registration & Membership allows you to sync registration data directly with Kit (formerly ConvertKit), so you can build your email list and run targeted campaigns without manual work.

This tutorial will show you how to connect your Kit account to User Registration forms and automatically subscribe new users to your email lists.

**Requirements:** Connecting Kit requires the **ConvertKit addon**, available with **Personal plan or higher**. You'll also need an active Kit account with API credentials.

## Getting Your Kit API Credentials

Before connecting Kit to your registration forms, you'll need to get your API Key and API Secret from your Kit account.

To get your API credentials, log in to your Kit account and click your **Account Name** in the top right corner. Then, go to **Settings > Developer > API Keys**.

Here, you'll see your API Key and API Secret. Copy both — you'll need them in the next step.

## Installing and Activating the ConvertKit Addon

Once you have your API credentials, go ahead and install the ConvertKit addon.

From your WordPress dashboard, navigate to **User Registration & Membership > Addons**. Search for "Kit" and toggle the switch to activate the addon.

If you purchased User Registration Premium, you can also download the ConvertKit addon from your WPEverest account page and upload it via **Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin**.

## Connecting Your Kit Account

Now that the addon is active, you can connect your Kit account to User Registration.

From the WordPress dashboard, go to **User Registration > Settings > Integration > ConvertKit**.

Enter your **API Key** and **API Secret** that you copied earlier. You can also add an **Account Name** — this can be anything you choose to help you identify the connection.

Then, click **Connect** to link your Kit account.

Once connected, you'll be able to select Kit forms and tags when configuring individual registration forms.

## Mapping Form Fields to Kit

With your Kit account connected, you can now map your registration form fields to Kit subscriber fields.

Go to **User Registration & Membership > All Forms** and click **Edit** on the form you want to connect. Navigate to **Form Settings > Integration > ConvertKit** and click **Add Connection**.

Give your connection a name (this is for internal reference only) and click **Add Connection**.

Here, you'll configure how registration data is sent to Kit:

**Action to Perform:** Choose **Subscribe** to add contacts to your mailing list, or **Unsubscribe** to remove contacts from your list. When you select Subscribe, you'll need to map the Email field — this is required. When you select Unsubscribe, contacts are removed from your Kit list without deleting their site account information.

**Select Form:** Choose which Kit form to link to your User Registration form. This determines which Kit list receives new subscribers.

**Select Tags:** Choose tags from your Kit dashboard to segment subscribers for targeted campaigns. Tags help you organize contacts based on their interests or behavior.

**Email Field Mapping:** This is required when using the Subscribe action. Select which registration form field contains the user's email address.

**First Name Field Mapping:** Optionally map the user's first name to personalize your Kit emails.

## Using Conditional Logic for Audience Segmentation

If you'd like to send registration data to Kit only when certain conditions are met, you can enable conditional logic.

Toggle on **Use Conditional Logic** and configure rules based on form field values. For example, you could subscribe users to different Kit forms based on their interests, membership level, or other selections they make during registration.

Conditional logic evaluates form values in real-time, allowing sophisticated audience segmentation without manual work.

## Testing Your Kit Integration

Before going live, we recommend testing your Kit connection by submitting a test registration.

Fill out your registration form and submit it. Then, check your Kit account to confirm the new subscriber appears in the correct form with the appropriate tags.

If the subscriber doesn't appear, double-check that your API credentials are correct and that the Email field mapping is configured properly.

## Klaviyo Integration

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/klaviyo-integration>

Klaviyo Integration for User Registration & Membership

# Klaviyo Integration
Pro Automatically sync new member registrations to Klaviyo email lists for targeted campaigns and marketing automation without manual data entry.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to automatically add new members to your Klaviyo email lists when they register on your site? User Registration & Membership allows you to sync registration data directly with Klaviyo, so you can send targeted email campaigns and automate your marketing workflows without manual data entry.

This tutorial will show you how to connect your Klaviyo account to User Registration & Membership and map your registration form fields to Klaviyo subscriber lists.

**Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin on your WordPress site.** Then, make sure you have an active Klaviyo account with at least one subscriber list created. Then, go to **User Registration & Membership **> **Addons, **search for Klaviyo and toggle to enable it.

## Getting Your Klaviyo API Key

To connect User Registration & Membership with Klaviyo, you'll need a Private API Key from your Klaviyo account.

Log in to your Klaviyo account and click your **Account Name** in the bottom left corner.

From the dropdown menu, go to **Settings > Account > API Keys**.

Click the **Create Private API Key** button.

Klaviyo will ask you to provide a name for this key—you can use something like "URM Integration" to help you remember what it's for.

For the access level, choose **Full Access Key**. This permission level is required for the integration to work properly. Click **Create** to generate your API key.

Copy the API key that appears. You'll need to paste this into your WordPress site in the next step.

Keep your API key secure and never share it publicly. This key gives access to your Klaviyo account data.

## Connecting Klaviyo to User Registration & Membership

Once you have your API key, go to your WordPress dashboard and navigate to **User Registration & Membership > Settings > Integration > Klaviyo**.

Paste your API key into the **API Key** field. In the **Account Name** field, enter any name you'd like—this is just for your reference and can be anything that helps you identify this connection (for example, "Main Klaviyo Account").

Click **Connect** to link your Klaviyo account with User Registration & Membership. Once connected, you'll see a confirmation message.

## Mapping Form Fields to Klaviyo

Now that your accounts are connected, you can map your registration form fields to Klaviyo subscriber lists.

Go to **User Registration & Membership > All Forms** and click **Edit** on the registration form you want to connect to Klaviyo.

Navigate to **Form Settings > Integration > Klaviyo** and click **Add New Connection**.

Provide a connection name—this is an internal label to help you identify this integration if you have multiple Klaviyo connections. Click **Add Connection** to continue.

You'll now see the field mapping interface. Here, you'll map your User Registration form fields to the corresponding fields in your Klaviyo subscriber list:

**Select List**: Choose which Klaviyo subscriber list you want to send registration data to

**Email Address**: Map your registration form's email field to Klaviyo's email field (required)

**First Name**: Map your form's first name field to Klaviyo's first name field (optional)

**Last Name**: Map your form's last name field to Klaviyo's last name field (optional)

The email field mapping is required—without it, Klaviyo won't be able to create subscriber records.

## Configuring Sync Options

Below the field mapping, you'll see additional sync options:

**Sync Klaviyo on User Update**: When enabled, any changes users make to their profile information in the My Account page will automatically sync to their Klaviyo contact record. This keeps your email list data current without manual updates.

**Unsubscribe on User Deletion**: When enabled, users who are deleted from your WordPress site will automatically be removed from your Klaviyo subscriber list. This helps you maintain a clean email list and comply with data privacy requirements.

## Using Conditional Logic (Optional)

If you'd like to send registration data to Klaviyo only when certain conditions are met, you can enable conditional logic.

Click the dropdown arrow next to your Klaviyo connection name and select **Enable Conditional Logic**. This opens the conditional logic builder where you can add rules based on form field values.

For example, you could send data to Klaviyo only if a user selects "Yes" on a newsletter opt-in checkbox, or only if they choose a specific membership plan.

Add your conditions using the logic builder, then save your form settings.

## Testing Your Integration

To verify everything is working correctly, submit a test registration through your form. Then, log in to your Klaviyo account and check your subscriber list—you should see the new contact appear with the mapped field data.

## LearnDash

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/learndash>

LearnDash Auto-Enrollment for User Registration & Membership

# LearnDash
Pro Automatically enroll users in LearnDash courses through custom registration forms with instant access upon signup.
Last updated on Jul 17, 2026

Would you like to automatically enroll users in LearnDash courses when they register on your site? User Registration & Membership allows you to create custom registration forms that connect directly to LearnDash, so users can select courses during signup and gain instant access. This tutorial will show you how to set up the LearnDash integration and configure automatic course enrollment.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you've installed and activated the LearnDash LMS plugin.

**Requirements:** The LearnDash integration requires the LearnDash addon, available with Plus or Professional plans.

## Installing and Activating the LearnDash Addon

To connect User Registration & Membership with LearnDash, you'll need to activate the LearnDash addon first.

Go to **User Registration & Membership > Addons** in your WordPress dashboard. Here, you'll see a list of all available addons organized by category. Locate the LearnDash addon and toggle the switch to **Activate**.

Once activated, the LearnDash integration features will be available in your registration forms.

## Adding the LearnDash Field to Your Registration Form

The LearnDash field allows users to select courses or groups during registration. You can add this field to any new or existing registration form.

Go to **User Registration & Membership > Add New** to create a new registration form, or edit an existing form. In the form builder, you'll see the LearnDash field available in the field palette on the left side.

Drag the **LearnDash** field from the palette and drop it into your form. By default, the form includes User Email and User Password fields — the LearnDash field will appear alongside your other registration fields.

Click on the LearnDash field to access **Field Options** in the left sidebar.

## Configuring the LearnDash Field

Once you've added the LearnDash field, you'll need to configure how it works.

In **Field Options > Advanced Settings**, locate the **Enroll Type** dropdown. Here, you can choose between two options:

**Courses** — Users can select individual LearnDash courses

**Groups** — Users can select LearnDash groups

Select the enroll type that matches your setup. If you want users to choose from individual courses, select **Courses**. If you've organized your courses into LearnDash groups, select **Groups**.

You can also configure the field type. The LearnDash field can display as either a **select field** (dropdown) or **checkbox** (allowing multiple selections). Choose the option that works best for your registration flow.

Click **Update Form** to save your changes.

## Setting Up Automatic Course Enrollment

User Registration & Membership can automatically enroll users in specific courses when they register — no manual intervention required.

Go to **User Registration & Membership > All Forms** and click **Edit** on the form you want to configure. Navigate to **Form Settings > LearnDash LMS**.

Here, you'll see the **Automatically enroll courses** option. Click the dropdown and select the courses you want all users to be enrolled in when they submit this form. You can select multiple courses.

Click **Update Form** to save your settings. Now, every user who registers through this form will be automatically enrolled in the selected courses.

Courses set to 'Open' Access Mode in LearnDash will automatically enroll users even if not selected in these settings. To exclude courses from automatic enrollment, set them to Premium or Closed Access Mode in LearnDash.

## Configuring Conditional Course Enrollment

If you'd prefer to enroll users in courses based on conditions they meet during registration, you can use conditional enrollment.

Go to **Form Settings > LearnDash LMS** and enable **Assign LearnDash course Conditionally**. Once enabled, you'll see options to create conditions.

Click **Add Condition** to create your first rule. You can set conditions based on any field in your registration form. For example, you might enroll users in different courses based on their selected membership plan, their role, or their responses to specific form fields.

For each condition, select:

The form field to evaluate

The comparison operator (equals, contains, etc.)

The value to match

The courses to enroll users in when the condition is met

You can create multiple conditions to handle different enrollment scenarios. Click **Update Form** to save your conditional enrollment rules.

## Controlling Course Access Mode in LearnDash

LearnDash courses have an Access Mode setting that affects how automatic enrollment works with User Registration & Membership.

To change a course's Access Mode, go to **LearnDash LMS > Courses** in your WordPress dashboard. Select the course you want to configure and click **Settings**.

In the course settings, locate the **Access Mode** option. You'll see three choices:

**Open** — Anyone can access the course without enrollment

**Premium** — Users must be enrolled to access the course

**Closed** — Users must be enrolled to access the course

If you set a course to **Open**, users will be automatically enrolled even if you haven't selected it in your automatic enrollment settings. To prevent this, set the course to **Premium** or **Closed** Access Mode.

Click **Update** to save the course settings.

## Replacing Default LearnDash Login and Registration

By default, LearnDash uses its own login and registration pages. You can replace these with your User Registration forms for a consistent experience.

First, disable LearnDash's built-in login and registration. Go to **LearnDash LMS > Settings** and locate the **General > Appearance > Login & Registration **and disbale it.

Next, configure your User Registration forms as the default login and registration pages. Go to **User Registration & Membership > Settings > General > Pages** and select your registration page from the **Registration Page** dropdown. Select your login page from the **Login Page** dropdown.

Click **Save Changes**. Now, when users try to access LearnDash courses, they'll be directed to your custom User Registration forms instead of the default LearnDash pages.

## Viewing Course Details in My Account

Users can view their enrolled LearnDash courses directly from their User Registration & Membership account page.

Once the LearnDash addon is activated, a **LearnDash** tab automatically appears in the My Account page. Users can click this tab to see:

All courses they're enrolled in

Course progress and completion status

Course expiry dates (if applicable)

Links to access their courses

No additional configuration is needed — the LearnDash tab appears automatically for users who have registered through User Registration & Membership forms.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Can users select multiple courses during registration?**

Yes. If you configure the LearnDash field as a checkbox field, users can select multiple courses. If you use a select field (dropdown), users can only choose one course.

**What happens if I change a course's Access Mode after users are enrolled?**

Changing the Access Mode won't affect users who are already enrolled. They'll retain access to the course. The Access Mode only affects new enrollments.

**Can I enroll users in both courses and groups?**

Not in the same field. The LearnDash field can be set to either Courses or Groups mode. If you need both, add two separate LearnDash fields to your form — one for courses and one for groups.

**Do users need to complete payment before being enrolled in courses?**

If your form includes payment fields, enrollment happens after successful payment. If your form is free, enrollment happens immediately after registration.

## Mailchimp

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/mailchimp>

Mailchimp Integration for User Registration & Membership

# Mailchimp
Pro Automatically sync new user registrations with Mailchimp email lists to streamline your email marketing without manual data entry.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to automatically add new users to your Mailchimp email lists when they register on your site? User Registration & Membership allows you to sync registration data directly with Mailchimp, so you can build your email marketing lists without manual work. This tutorial will show you how to connect Mailchimp to your registration forms and configure the integration.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership plugin. Then, make sure you've installed and activated the Mailchimp addon from **User Registration & Membership > Addons **(available with Personal plan or higher).

You'll also need an active Mailchimp account with at least one audience list created.

## Getting Your Mailchimp API Key

To connect User Registration & Membership with Mailchimp, you'll need your API key and username from your Mailchimp account.

Log in to your Mailchimp account and click on your profile name in the top right corner.

From the dropdown menu, go to **Extras > API Keys**.

On the API Keys page, click **Create A Key**.

Give your API key a descriptive name so you can identify it later, then click **Generate Key**. Once the key is generated, copy it to your clipboard — you'll need this in the next step.

Keep your API key secure. Never share it publicly or commit it to version control systems.

## Connecting Mailchimp to User Registration & Membership

Now that you have your API key, you can connect Mailchimp to the plugin.

In your WordPress dashboard, go to **User Registration & Membership > Settings > Integration > Mailchimp**. Paste your API key into the API Key field, then enter your Mailchimp username in the Username field. Click **Connect** to establish the connection.

Once connected, you'll see a confirmation message. Your Mailchimp account is now linked to User Registration & Membership, and you can start syncing users to your email lists.

## Adding Mailchimp to a Registration Form

With Mailchimp connected at the global level, you can now configure individual registration forms to send data to specific Mailchimp lists.

Go to **User Registration & Membership > All Forms** and either create a new form or edit an existing one. Make sure you add a** Checkbox field**, if you want to use Conditional Logic for Mailchimp integration.

Navigate to **Form Settings > Mailchimp > Integration** and click **Add New Connection**.

Give your connection a descriptive name (this is for internal reference only) and click **Add Connection**. This opens the connection configuration panel where you'll map your form fields to Mailchimp.

## Mapping Form Fields to Mailchimp

Field mapping tells User Registration & Membership which form data to send to which Mailchimp fields.

In the connection settings, you'll see options to map your form fields to Mailchimp list fields. Make sure the data types match between your form fields and Mailchimp fields — for example, email fields should map to email fields, text fields to text fields, and so on.

To verify your Mailchimp field types, log in to Mailchimp and go to **Audience > Settings > Audience fields and |MERGE| tags**. This shows you the exact field structure of your Mailchimp list.

## Adding Tags to Organize Subscribers

Tags help you organize and segment your Mailchimp subscribers based on where they registered or what they're interested in.

In the Mailchimp connection settings, you can add tags to automatically label new subscribers. You can select existing tags from your Mailchimp account or create new ones directly from the plugin interface.

Tags are custom labels that help you identify and segment subscribers. For example, you might tag users who register through a specific form as "Website Signup" or "Premium Members."

**Use Double Optin: **If you want to send a verification message to users before subscribing, check the ‘Use double option’ checkbox.

**Sync Mailchimp on user update: **Enable this option to sync the user’s data to Mailchimp when the users update their profile details from the My Account page.

**Unsubscribe on user deletion:** Enable this option to delete the user’s contact from the Mailchimp account then their account is deleted from the site.

## Using Conditional Logic for Audience Segmentation

Conditional logic lets you send users to different Mailchimp lists or apply different tags based on their form responses.

Enable **Use Conditional Logic** in the connection settings to set up rules. You can create conditions based on any form field value — for example, send users who select "Premium Plan" to one list and users who select "Basic Plan" to another.

Conditional logic evaluates form field values in real-time during registration, allowing sophisticated audience segmentation without manual sorting.

## Adding Users to Mailchimp Groups

Mailchimp groups let you organize subscribers within a single list based on their interests or preferences.

In the Mailchimp connection settings, you can select which Mailchimp groups to add users to automatically. Groups you've created in your Mailchimp account will appear in the dropdown menu.

Groups are different from tags — groups are visible to subscribers and often used for preference management, while tags are internal labels for your organization.

## Testing Your Mailchimp Integration

Before going live, test your Mailchimp integration to make sure data flows correctly.

Submit a test registration through your form using a real email address you can access. Then, log in to your Mailchimp account and check your audience list. The test user should appear in your contacts with the correct field data, tags, and group assignments.

If the user doesn't appear, check your connection settings and field mappings. Make sure your API key is valid and your Mailchimp account is active.

## MailerLite

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/mailerlite>

MailerLite

# MailerLite
Pro Integrate MailerLite with registration forms to automatically add new users to email lists and marketing campaigns.
Last updated on Aug 12, 2026

Would you like to automatically add new registrants to your MailerLite email lists? User Registration & Membership makes it easy to connect your registration forms with MailerLite, so every new user is automatically added to your email marketing campaigns. This tutorial will show you how to install and use the MailerLite addon with User Registration & Membership.

Before getting started, make sure you have installed and activated the User Registration & Membership plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you have installed and activated the MailerLite addon.

**The MailerLite addon is available with Plus or Professional plans.**

## Activating the MailerLite Addon

To activate the MailerLite addon, go to **User Registration & Membership > Addons** in your WordPress dashboard. Here, you'll see a list of all available addons.

Find the MailerLite addon in the list and toggle the switch to activate it. Once activated, you can proceed to connect your MailerLite account.

## Connecting Your MailerLite Account

To connect your MailerLite account, go to **User Registration & Membership > Settings > Integration > Email Marketing > MailerLite**. Here, you'll configure the connection between your WordPress site and MailerLite.

You'll need your MailerLite API key to complete the connection. To get your API key:

Log in to your MailerLite account

Navigate to Integrations > Developer API

Click Generate new token

Give your token a name and click Create token

Copy the generated API key

Once you have your API key, paste it into the API Key field in User Registration & Membership > Settings > Integration > MailerLite. Click Save Changes to connect your account.

Once connected, you'll see a success message confirming the connection.

## Adding MailerLite to a Registration Form

To add MailerLite integration to a registration form, create or edit a form to open the form builder. Then, go to **Form Settings > Integration> MailerLite.**

Click **Add New Connection** to create a new MailerLite connection for this form. You'll see a popup where you can configure the connection.

Enter a nickname for this connection. This is for your reference only and won't be visible to users. Then, select the MailerLite group you want to add subscribers to from the Group dropdown.

If you don't see your groups in the dropdown, make sure you've created groups in your MailerLite account first.

## Mapping Form Fields to MailerLite

After selecting your group, you'll need to map your registration form fields to MailerLite fields. This tells the addon which information from your form should be sent to which field in MailerLite.

The Email field is required and will be mapped automatically. For additional fields:

Select a form field from the left dropdown

Select the corresponding MailerLite field from the right dropdown

Click the + button to add more field mappings

Common field mappings include First Name, Last Name, and Phone. You can map as many fields as you need.

Custom fields must be created in your MailerLite account before they appear in the mapping dropdown.

## Use Double Opt-in

Enable the **Use Double Opt-in** option if you want MailerLite to send a confirmation email before subscribing users. Users will only be added to your MailerLite audience after they verify their email address.

## Using Conditional Logic

If you'd like to control when users are added to MailerLite based on their form responses, toggle on Enable Conditional Logic.

Once enabled, you can set conditions like:

Only add users who select a specific option from a dropdown

Only add users who check a newsletter subscription checkbox

Only add users based on their selected user role

Click Add Condition to create your first rule. Select the form field, choose the condition type, and enter the value to match.

## Testing Your MailerLite Connection

After configuring your MailerLite connection, click Save to save your settings. Then, we recommend testing the connection by submitting a test registration.

To test:

Open your registration form on the front end

Fill out the form with test information

Submit the form

Check your MailerLite account to verify the subscriber was added

If the subscriber appears in your MailerLite group with the correct information, your connection is working correctly.

## Managing Multiple MailerLite Connections

You can add multiple MailerLite connections to a single form. This is useful if you want to add users to different groups based on their selections.

To add another connection, click Add New Connection again in Form Settings > MailerLite. Each connection can have its own group selection, field mapping, and conditional logic.

To edit an existing connection, click the edit icon next to the connection name. To delete a connection, click the delete icon.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why don't I see my MailerLite groups in the dropdown?

Make sure you've created groups in your MailerLite account first. Then, verify your API key is entered correctly in User Registration & Membership > Settings > Integration > MailerLite. If groups still don't appear, try disconnecting and reconnecting your account.

### Can I add users to multiple groups at once?

Yes. Create multiple MailerLite connections in your form settings, each pointing to a different group. Users will be added to all groups when they submit the form.

### What happens if a user is already in my MailerLite group?

MailerLite will update the existing subscriber with any new information from the form. Duplicate subscribers are not created.

### Can I use conditional logic to add users to different groups?

Yes. Create multiple MailerLite connections, each with different conditional logic rules. Users will only be added to groups where they meet the conditions.

That's it! Now you know how to connect User Registration & Membership with MailerLite. Next, would you like to learn how to segment your email lists based on user roles or membership levels? Be sure to check out our guide on using conditional logic with the MailerLite addon for all the details.

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/mailpoet-integration>

MailPoet Integration for User Registration & Membership

# MailPoet Integration
Pro Automatically sync new user registrations with MailPoet email lists, eliminating manual subscriber imports and streamlining your email marketing workflow.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to automatically add new users to your MailPoet email lists when they register on your site? User Registration & Membership allows you to connect your registration forms directly to MailPoet, so every new signup becomes an email subscriber without manual imports. This tutorial will show you how to set up and configure the MailPoet integration.

**Before getting started**, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you've installed and activated the MailPoet plugin and have at least one subscriber list created in MailPoet.

## MailPoet Configuration

Go to **WPDashboard > MailPoet** and click on the **Begin Setup** button.

After you click onthe **Begin Setup** button, you will be redirected to next page and tick mark the Confirm privacy and data settings as shown below.

Click on **Continue**, tick mark if you want to power up your WooCommerce store, and click on **Continue**.

Click on the **Connect MailPoet **button.

Now, you will be redirected to the MailPoet Account Page.

Either login to your MailPoet Account or create a new account .

Once you’re logged in, you have to add a **plan**, provide the details of the website, and **activate **it.

You will see the below interface once you **activate **the plan.

Copy this key to your clipboard and enter it to activate the **MailPoet account.**

Once you have entered the activation key, now you will connected to the **MailPoet **as shown below.

## Activating the MailPoet Module

To use MailPoet with User Registration & Membership, you'll first need to activate the integration module.

Go to **User Registration & Membership → Addons** in your WordPress dashboard. Here, you'll see a list of available modules and integrations. Locate the MailPoet addon and toggle the switch to activate it.

Once activated, the MailPoet integration settings will become available in your plugin configuration.

## Connecting Your MailPoet Account

After activating the module, you need to connect User Registration & Membership to your MailPoet installation.

Navigate to **User Registration & Membership → Settings → Integration → Email Marketing → MailPoet**. You'll see a connection option labeled "Check to connect your MailPoet Account." Enable this option by checking the box, then click **Save Changes**.

Your User Registration & Membership plugin is now connected to MailPoet and ready to sync subscriber data.

## Mapping Form Fields to MailPoet Lists

Now you'll configure which registration forms send data to MailPoet and which subscriber lists receive that data.

Go to **User Registration & Membership → All Forms** and click **Edit** on the registration form you want to connect to MailPoet. Navigate to **Form Settings → Integration→ MailPoet **and click **Add New Connection**.

In the connection settings, you'll configure how form data flows to MailPoet:

**Select MailPoet List**: Choose the subscriber list where new registrations should be added. This list must already exist in your MailPoet dashboard.

**Email Address Field**: Map the email field from your registration form to MailPoet. This field is mandatory — MailPoet requires an email address to create a subscriber.

**First Name Field**: Optionally map the first name field from your registration form to MailPoet's first name field. This helps personalize your email campaigns.

**Last Name Field**: Optionally map the last name field to MailPoet's last name field for additional personalization.

Once you've configured the field mappings, click **Save** to activate the connection.

## Using Conditional Logic for Audience Segmentation

If you'd prefer to add users to different MailPoet lists based on their form responses, you can enable conditional logic.

In the same connection settings screen, enable the **Use Conditional Logic** option. This allows you to create rules that evaluate form field values in real-time during registration.

For example, you could send users who select "Newsletter" in a checkbox field to one list, while users who select "Product Updates" go to a different list. Conditional logic enables sophisticated audience segmentation without requiring users to manually choose their subscriber preferences.

Conditional logic evaluates form values as users submit the registration form, so your rules must be based on fields that exist in your form.

## Testing Your Integration

After configuring the MailPoet connection, test it by submitting a registration through your form.

Create a test user account using your registration form. After submission, log into your MailPoet dashboard and navigate to your subscriber lists. The new user should appear in the list you selected during configuration, with their email address and any mapped fields (first name, last name) populated correctly.

If the subscriber doesn't appear, check that:

The MailPoet module is activated in User Registration & Membership → Addons

The connection is enabled in Settings → Integration → MailPoet

The correct MailPoet list is selected in your form's integration settings

The email field mapping is configured (this is required)
