## Masteriyo LMS Integration

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/masteriyo-lms-integration>

Masteriyo LMS Integration for Membership Website | URM Docs

# Masteriyo LMS Integration
Pro Extend membership features by integrating Masteriyo LMS to provide course access alongside content, combining robust course creation with membership management.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

The Masteriyo integration helps in expanding your membership features, by providing online course access alongide your other content. Combining the awesome course creation capabilities of Masteriyo LMS (Which is a free, LMS plugin created by our own team) and our membership management ensures a robust experience for users.

## **Requirements:**

Free version of User Registration & Memberships plugin installed and activated

Free version of Masteriyo LMS installed and activated

## **Masteriyo Installation:**

Masteriyo LMS is free and can be installed to your WordPresss website by navigating from Plugins > Add new and searching for ‘Masteriyo’

You may now click on the install now button to install Masteriyo LMS. After that, you may click on the button again to activate the plugin.

After this, you will be redirected to the setup wizard for Masteriyo LMS. To keep things simple, in the “What’ I’ll need” section, ensure nothing is checked. For others, you may fill those out to your liking.

In the starter templates section, you may simply skip this too.

In the last step, choose if you’d want to install sample courses. You may choose, anything as you wish. We can always remove the sample courses later.

To create a course in Masteriyo, checkout: https://docs.masteriyo.com/course-creation/complete-course-creation

## **Important Configurations:**

Proceeding further, we will assume you have created a course in Masteriyo LMS. For the integration to work properly, ensure these settings are configured:

### **Course Pricing Settings:**

To configure course pricings, go to > Courses > Edit course (The course you have created) > Settings > Pricing:

Currently the integration works with “Requires registration to access” courses. Meaning, these courses can be given access to via memberships.

What about Free – open access and Paid courses?

The free courses, have no restrictions so they can be accessed by anyone. While, paid courses simply don’t show up, since User Registration & Membership will handle the paywall via memberships, so we cannot use the Masteriyo checkout system.

### **Masteriyo Registration configuration:**

Navigate to: Masteriyo > Settings > General > Registration, here you will see options to configure Masteriyo registration and checkout behavior.

Simply uncheck ‘Enable Student Registration’, ‘Enable Instructor Registration’ and ‘Enable Guest Checkout’. Since User Registration & Membership will handle the paywall and course access, Masteriyo registration and checkout will no longer be of use.

## **Addon activation:**

To properly activate the integration between the 2 plugins, navigate to User Registration & Membership > Addons > Masteriyo – Enable it.

## **Giving course access to Memberships:**

Now that you have Masteriyo LMS ready with course/s, Ensure you have created memberships too. Doc link: https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/docs/user-registration-membership-guide/#0-toc-title

Now to give access to courses, you may edit a membership. From User Registration > Memberships menu.

In the access tab for the membership, you will now be able to add “Masteriyo Courses” as content for the Membership.

Only courses with the pricing set to: Registration required to access will be visible in the drop down, since those are the only ones supported.

## **User Journey when purchasing Membership Courses**

Now if you checkout your courses page at: yourdomainname/courses, you will see a join now button next to the courses that are assigned to memberships.

When users click on Join now via the courses page, they will now see a radio select for the memberships that the course is a part of, in the single course page. Users can now select the membership plan and click on Sign Up, which will take them to the checkout for

When sign up is clicked, they will now be redirected to the User Registration & Membership Registration / Checkout page where the selected membership will be selected – ready for checkout.

## **Learning journey for users:**

Upon checkout from the registration page and successful payment completion, once the user has access to their membership and the content, they can now start their course from the following areas:

Courses page:
Now users will see a “Start Course” button instead of the “Join now” button like it was before.

My account page / Course Portal area:
In the URM my account page we will now have a My Courses section, from where users can view the courses they are enrolled into and start.

For more details regarding the courses, like quiz, assignments and other course details, users can visit the course-portal page. This is originally the Masteriyo My account page, where unnecessary info has been hidden. Making it a course focused extension of the URM account Page.

## **Handling Membership Upgrades for memberships with courses:**

To learn more about Membership Upgrade paths, please checkout this doc: https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/docs/how-to-set-up-membership-upgrade-in-wordpress/

Suppose a user wants to access a certain course that is not a part of their membership, but is a part of an upgraded membership, they may simply upgrade their membership from the membership pricing page.

The single course page will also show them the membership selector with the button text “Upgrade now”, since they will be upgrading their membership.

After this, the regular checkout process will occur and a user with the proper membership will be able to access the course.

Oxygen Builder Integration | URM Docs

# Oxygen Builder
Learn how to add and customize User Registration forms and login pages using Oxygen Builder's visual editor without coding.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to design custom registration and login pages using Oxygen Builder's visual editor? User Registration & Membership integrates seamlessly with Oxygen Builder Pro, allowing you to add registration forms, login forms, and user account features to your pages without writing code. This tutorial will show you how to add and customize User Registration blocks in Oxygen Builder.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated both the User Registration & Membership plugin and Oxygen Builder Pro on your WordPress site.

## Opening the Oxygen Builder Editor

To begin editing a page with Oxygen Builder, go to your WordPress dashboard and navigate to the Pages section. Find the page you want to edit and hover below the page name. Click 'Edit with Oxygen' to open Oxygen's visual page builder.

Once the Oxygen Builder interface loads, you'll see your page canvas in the center with editing tools on the left side.

## Adding User Registration Blocks

To add a User Registration block to your page, click the **plus** icon in the top left corner of the Oxygen Builder interface. This opens the module sidebar showing all available blocks and elements.

Scroll down the sidebar until you locate the User Registration menu section. Here, you'll find all available User Registration blocks that you can add to your page.

Before adding a User Registration block, you'll need to add a section to your page first. Click on any User Registration block from the menu—your options include Registration Form, Login Form, My Account, Edit Profile, Edit Password, View Profile Details, and Popup.

## Available User Registration Blocks

Oxygen Builder provides access to seven different User Registration blocks:

Registration Form — displays your custom registration forms

Login Form — adds a login form to any page

My Account — shows the user account dashboard

Edit Profile — allows users to update their profile information

Edit Password — provides a password change interface

View Profile Details — displays user profile information

Popup — adds popup functionality to your forms

## Customizing Block Styling

After adding a User Registration block to your page, you can customize its appearance using Oxygen Builder's styling options. All User Registration blocks support both Primary and Advanced styling customization.

Primary styling options allow you to customize the form container, labels, and buttons. These settings control the basic visual appearance of your registration or login forms.

Advanced styling options provide deeper customization capabilities. You can modify background colors, adjust size and spacing, change typography, add borders, and even include custom CSS and JavaScript.

The Advanced options also include layout settings to control how your form elements are arranged on the page.

## Requirements and Compatibility

This integration requires Oxygen Builder Pro—the free version of Oxygen Builder is not compatible with User Registration blocks. Make sure you have the Pro version installed before attempting to add User Registration features to your pages.

That's it! Now you know how to add and customize User Registration forms and features using Oxygen Builder's visual editor. Next, would you like to learn more about customizing individual form fields or configuring form settings? Be sure to check out our complete guide to the User Registration form builder for all the details.

## Salesforce Integration

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/salesforce-integration>

Salesforce Integration for User Registration & Membership

# Salesforce Integration
Pro Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to automatically sync your WordPress registration data with Salesforce CRM? User Registration & Membership allows you to connect your registration forms directly to Salesforce, sending user information to your CRM as leads, contacts, or accounts without manual data entry. This tutorial will show you how to set up and configure the Salesforce integration.

Before getting started, make sure you have installed and activated the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you have installed and activated the Salesforce addon from **User Registration & Membership > Addons > Salesforce**.

## Creating a Salesforce Connected App

To connect WordPress with Salesforce, you need to create a Connected App in your Salesforce account. This app generates the API credentials required for authentication.

From your Salesforce dashboard, click the settings icon in the top right corner and select Open Advanced Setup.

Once the setup page opens, navigate to Apps in the left sidebar, then click App Manager. Click the **New Connected App **button in the top right corner.

Choose **Create a Connected App** and click Continue.

Fill in the basic app information including the Connected App Name and your contact email address.

Next, enable OAuth Settings by checking the box. You need to retrieve your Callback URL from WordPress before proceeding.

Go to User Registration & Membership → Settings → Integration → Salesforce in your WordPress dashboard. Copy the Callback URL displayed on this page.

Return to Salesforce and paste the Callback URL into the appropriate field.

Under OAuth Scopes, add two required permissions: Manage user data via APIs and Perform requests at any time. Move these scopes from Available OAuth Scopes to Selected OAuth Scopes.

Uncheck the **Require Proof Key for Code Exchange** option. This setting must be disabled for the integration to work properly.

Click Save to create your Connected App. Salesforce requires a 10-minute waiting period before you can retrieve your API credentials. After waiting, click Continue.

## Retrieving Your API Credentials

Once the waiting period is complete, click **Manage Consumer Details** on your Connected App page.

Salesforce will send a verification code to your email address. Check your inbox and enter the code when prompted.

After verification, Salesforce displays your Consumer Key and Consumer Secret. Copy both values and keep them secure.

## Connecting WordPress to Salesforce

Return to your WordPress dashboard and navigate to User Registration & Membership → Settings → Integration → Salesforce. Paste your Consumer Key into the Consumer Key field and your Consumer Secret into the Consumer Secret field.

Enter a name for your Salesforce account in the Account Name field. This name is for your reference only and can be anything you choose.

Click the Authenticate with Salesforce button. You will be redirected to Salesforce to authorize the connection. Log in to your Salesforce account if prompted and click **Allow **to grant WordPress access to your Salesforce data.

After authorization, Salesforce redirects you back to WordPress with an access code. Copy this access code from the URL or the page display. Paste the access code into the Access Code field in WordPress and click Verify Accesscode.

Once verified, your WordPress site is successfully connected to Salesforce.

## Mapping Form Fields to Salesforce

Now that authentication is complete, you can configure which registration form data syncs to Salesforce. Go to User Registration & Membership → All Forms and select the form you want to connect.

Navigate to **Form Settings → Integration → Salesforce** and click **Add New Connection**. Give your connection a descriptive name and select your connected Salesforce account from the dropdown.

Choose which Salesforce objects to synchronize. You can select Leads, Contacts, or Accounts depending on how you want to organize your data in Salesforce.

Map your WordPress registration fields to the corresponding Salesforce fields. For each field in your registration form, select the matching Salesforce field from the dropdown. This ensures that user data flows into the correct Salesforce fields.

Field types must be compatible between WordPress and Salesforce for proper data transfer. For example, email fields should map to email fields, and text fields should map to text fields.

Click Update Form to save your configuration.

## Testing Your Integration

To verify that your integration works correctly, open your registration form in an incognito or private browser window. Fill out the form with test data and submit it.

Log in to your Salesforce account and navigate to your contact list or the object type you configured. The test submission should appear in Salesforce with all mapped fields populated correctly.

If data does not appear in Salesforce, verify that your field mappings are correct and that the Salesforce connection is still active in WordPress.

## Using Conditional Logic

You can enable conditional logic to control when data is sent to Salesforce based on user responses. This feature allows sophisticated audience segmentation during registration.

In your form settings under the Salesforce integration section, enable Use Conditional Logic. Configure rules that determine which form submissions sync to Salesforce based on specific field values or user selections.

That's it! Now you know how to integrate User Registration & Membership with Salesforce CRM. Next, would you like to explore other CRM integrations? Be sure to check out our guide on email marketing integrations for more ways to sync your user data.

## Woocommerce Integration

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/woocommerce-integration>

WooCommerce Integration Guide for User Registration Forms

# Woocommerce Integration
Pro Integrate WooCommerce with custom registration forms, add checkout fields, and sync user data to create seamless customer registration experiences.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to connect your WooCommerce store with custom registration forms and membership features? User Registration & Membership allows you to add custom fields to WooCommerce checkout, sync user data between systems, and create seamless registration experiences for your customers. This guide will show you how to set up and configure the WooCommerce integration.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you've installed and activated the WooCommerce plugin and the WooCommerce addon for User Registration & Membership.

## Activating the WooCommerce Addon

The WooCommerce addon is available with Plus and Professional plans of User Registration & Membership Pro.

To activate the WooCommerce addon, go to **User Registration & Membership > Addons**. Locate the WooCommerce addon in the list and toggle it to **Activate**. Once activated, you'll see new WooCommerce-specific options in your form builder and settings.

## Understanding WooCommerce Integration Features

The WooCommerce addon provides three main integration points:

**WooCommerce Fields in Registration Forms**: Add 23 WooCommerce-specific fields to your registration forms, including 10 shipping address fields and 13 billing address fields (country, name, company, address, city, state, postcode, phone, email, and separate shipping option).

**My Account Page Integration**: Display User Registration form data in the WooCommerce My Account page, with extra tabs for Orders, Downloads, and Addresses appearing automatically after activation.

**Checkout Page Sync**: Sync User Registration form fields with the WooCommerce checkout registration, allowing customers to create accounts during purchase with your custom fields.

## Adding WooCommerce Fields to Registration Forms

From the form builder, go to **User Registration & Membership > Forms > Edit Form**. In the form builder, you'll see WooCommerce fields available in the field palette once the addon is activated.

Drag and drop WooCommerce fields into your form. Available fields include:

**Billing Address Fields**: Billing Country, Billing First Name, Billing Last Name, Billing Company, Billing Address 1, Billing Address 2, Billing City, Billing State, Billing Postcode, Billing Email, Billing Phone

**Shipping Address Fields**: Shipping Country, Shipping First Name, Shipping Last Name, Shipping Company, Shipping Address 1, Shipping Address 2, Shipping City, Shipping State, Shipping Postcode, Separate Shipping Option

Once you've added the fields, click **Update Form** to save your changes.

## Integrating User Registration Forms with WooCommerce My Account

To display User Registration form data in the WooCommerce My Account page, go to **User Registration & Membership > Settings > WooCommerce**.

Select the registration form you want to integrate from the **Registration Form** dropdown. This determines which form's data will appear in the WooCommerce My Account page.

Click **Save Changes** to apply the integration.

If both WooCommerce and User Registration create separate My Account pages, you may see a conflict. To resolve this, go to **WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced** and select the User Registration Account Page as the **My account page**. This ensures users see a unified account experience.

## Replacing WooCommerce Login and Registration Pages

You can replace WooCommerce's default login and registration pages with User Registration forms for a consistent user experience.

First, go to **WooCommerce > Settings > Accounts and Privacy**. Check the option **Allow customers to create an account on the "My Account" page**.

Then, go to **User Registration & Membership > Integration > Settings > WooCommerce**. Select your registration form from the dropdown, then check **Replace default WooCommerce's login and registration page with User Registration forms**.

Click **Save Changes** to save your settings. Users will now see your custom User Registration forms instead of WooCommerce's default pages.

## Syncing Registration Fields with WooCommerce Checkout

To display User Registration form fields during WooCommerce checkout, go to **WooCommerce > Settings > Accounts and Privacy**. Check the option **Allow customers to create an account during checkout**.

Then, go to **User Registration & Membership > Settings > WooCommerce**. Check Sync the user registration form with the **WooCommerce checkout registration**.

Only custom User Registration fields that don't already exist in WooCommerce's default registration will appear at checkout. This prevents duplicate fields and keeps the checkout process clean.

### Alternative Method: Using the Sync Checkout Fields Block

You can also add specific fields to the checkout page using the Sync Checkout Fields block.

Navigate to **Pages** and open your Checkout page in the block editor. Add the **Sync Checkout Fields** block to the page.

In the block settings on the right, select which User Registration fields you want to display at checkout.

Click **Update** to save the page. The selected fields will now appear during the checkout registration process.

## Enabling Login Options at Checkout

If you'd like to use the login options from your User Registration form (such as social login or passwordless login) in the WooCommerce checkout, go to **User Registration & Membership > Settings > Integration > WooCommerce**.

After selecting your registration form, check **Enable Login Options** to sync login methods from your User Registration form to the checkout page.

Click **Save Changes** to apply this setting.

## Managing Billing and Shipping Addresses

Once the WooCommerce integration is active, users can edit their billing and shipping addresses directly from the My Account page.

Users navigate to the **Addresses** tab in their account dashboard. Here, they'll see options to edit both billing and shipping addresses. Any changes made here will sync with both WooCommerce and User Registration data.

## Integrating WooCommerce with Product Pages

You can map User Registration forms to specific WooCommerce products for product-specific registration.

Go to **Products** and select a product to edit. In the **Product Data** meta box, click the **UR Form** tab. Map your User Registration form to this product and select which fields should appear.

Click **Update** to save the product. When customers view or purchase this product, they'll see your custom registration fields.

## Content Restriction for WooCommerce Products

The WooCommerce integration works with User Registration's content restriction features to control product visibility and purchasability.

Product-specific access rules are evaluated to determine if users can see or purchase products. Restricted products can be hidden from shop loops and search results based on your access rules.

To configure product restrictions, go to **User Registration & Membership > Content Rules** and create rules that target WooCommerce products.

## Important Notes About WooCommerce Integration

Keep in mind these important details when using the WooCommerce integration:

The WooCommerce addon is only available for Plus and Professional plans

If you use a membership field in your registration form, Payment Fields cannot be used in the same form

Only custom User Registration fields that don't exist in WooCommerce's default registration are shown in checkout sync

Billing and shipping addresses can be edited from both the WooCommerce My Account page and the User Registration account page

Account page conflicts can occur when both plugins create separate My Account pages—resolve this by selecting one as the primary page in WooCommerce settings

## Zapier

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/integrations/zapier>

User Registration & Membership Zapier Integration

# Zapier
Pro Automate user registration workflows by connecting forms to 1,500+ apps through Zapier integration without coding.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to automatically send user registration data to thousands of other apps? User Registration & Membership allows you to connect your registration forms with Zapier, enabling you to automate workflows and sync data with over 1,500 apps without writing any code. This tutorial will show you how to set up and configure the Zapier integration.

Before getting started, make sure you have installed and activated the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin. The Zapier addon is available with Plus or Professional plan licenses. You will also need an active Zapier account.

## Activating the Zapier Addon

To begin using Zapier with your registration forms, you first need to activate the Zapier addon.

From your WordPress dashboard, go to User Registration & Membership > Addons. Locate the Zapier addon in the list and toggle the switch to Activate. Once activated, the Zapier integration settings will become available in your form settings.

## Creating a Zap in Zapier

A Zap is an automated workflow that connects your registration form to another app. To create a Zap, you need to set up a webhook connection between User Registration & Membership and Zapier.

Log into your Zapier account and click the **Make A Zap** button.

When prompted to choose a trigger app, search for and select **Webhooks by Zapier**.

For the Trigger Event, select Catch Hook.

Zapier will generate a custom Webhook URL for you. Copy this URL as you will need it in the next step.

## Connecting Your Registration Form to Zapier

Now that you have your webhook URL from Zapier, you can connect it to your registration form.

In WordPress, go to User Registration & Membership > Add New to create a new form, or select an existing form to edit. Once your form is open in the Form Builder, navigate to the Form Settings tab. Click on **Integration > Zapier **Settings to access the integration options.

Check the Enable Zapier option to activate the integration for this form. Paste the Webhook URL you copied from Zapier into the provided field. This URL tells your form where to send the registration data.

## Configuring Trigger Conditions

User Registration & Membership gives you control over when data is sent to Zapier. You can configure optional trigger conditions to determine exactly when the webhook fires.

In the Zapier Settings section, you will find three trigger options. Trigger hook only after user approval sends data to Zapier only after an admin approves the user registration. This is useful if you manually review registrations before granting access. Trigger hook on user profile update sends the webhook when an existing user updates their profile information. Trigger hook on WooCommerce checkout fires the webhook during the WooCommerce checkout process if you have WooCommerce integration enabled.

Enable the trigger conditions that match your workflow needs. You can enable multiple triggers if needed. Once configured, click Update to save your form settings.

## Testing the Connection

Before going live, you should test the connection to ensure data flows correctly from your registration form to Zapier.

Submit a sample form entry using your registration form. This sends test data to Zapier through the webhook. Return to Zapier and click Continue in your Zap setup.

Click Test Trigger to verify that Zapier received the form data.

If the test is successful, Zapier will display the data it received from your form.

Once the test passes, you can continue building your Zap by adding action steps that use the registration data.

## What Happens After Setup

After completing the setup, your registration form will automatically send data to Zapier whenever the configured trigger conditions are met. From Zapier, you can route this data to any of the 1,500+ connected apps to automate tasks like adding contacts to email lists, creating CRM records, sending notifications, or updating spreadsheets.

That's it! Now you know how to integrate Zapier with User Registration & Membership. Next, would you like to explore other integrations? Be sure to check out our guides on connecting with email marketing platforms like Mailchimp and ActiveCampaign for more ways to automate your member management.
